flags.finding: [partially supported] In S008 and S011, the production depicts a full vessel burning on open navigable waters using jerry cans of diesel fuel, blankets, flare gun ignition, and consumer/homemade mortar fireworks. In S008, the script itself explicitly states that the activity is an unpermitted maritime burn ('Open flame, on a vessel, in navigable waters. I checked. There's no permit on file. It's an unpermitted burn with a homemade pyrotechnics display'). Under CSATF Safety Bulletin #16 and maritime environmental safety regulations, an unpermitted open-water vessel burn using combustible diesel and unpermitted pyrotechnics is illegal and uninsurable as scripted without proper Authority Having Jurisdiction (AHJ) permits (USCG Captain of the Port, state environmental protection department, local municipal fire marshal) and a licensed Pyrotechnic Special Effects Operator. Production must engage a licensed pyrotechnician and obtain all requisite maritime burn and fireworks permits, or stage the burning vessel within a controlled water tank utilizing practical flame bars and VFX enhancements.

remedy.detail: Engage a state- and federally-licensed Pyrotechnic Special Effects Operator and certified Marine Fire Safety Officer to engineer the vessel burn; secure formal AHJ burn and pyrotechnic permits from the local Fire Department, State Environmental Protection Agency, and US Coast Guard Sector Command. Alternatively, execute the wide burning vessel shots via controlled burn on a steel barge/rig or VFX compositing, with close-ups shot on a controlled tank stage (remedy costs $15,000–$35,000 for pyrotechnician crew, permits, and standby fireboats, varying by shooting region and union agreements).

citations.excerpt: (3) PG-13 - Parents Strongly Cautioned. Some Material May Be Inappropriate For Children Under 13. A PG-13 rating is a sterner warning by the Rating Board to parents to determine whether their children under age 13 should view the motion picture, as some material might not be suited for them. A PG-13 motion picture may go beyond the PG rating in theme, violence, nudity, sensuality, language, adult activities or other elements, but does not reach the restricted R category. The theme of the motion picture by itself will not result in a rating greater than PG-13, although depictions of activities related to a mature theme may result in a restricted rating for the motion picture. Any drug use will initially require at least a PG-13 rating. More than brief nudity will require at least a PG-13 rating, but such nudity in a PG-13 rated motion picture generally will not be sexually oriented. There may be depictions of violence in a PG-13 movie, but generally not both realistic and extreme or persistent violence. A motion picture's single use of one of the harsher sexually-derived words, though only as an expletive, initially requires at least a PG-13 rating. More than one such expletive requires an R rating, as must even one of those words used in a sexual context. The Rating Board nevertheless may rate such a motion picture PG-13 if, based on a special vote by a two-thirds majority, the Raters feel that most American parents would believe that a PG-13 rating is appropriate because of the context or manner in which the words are used or because the use of those words in the motion picture is inconspicuous.

A PG-13 rating is a sterner warning by the Rating Board to parents to determine whether their children under age 13 should view the motion picture, as some material might not be suited for them. A PG-13 motion picture may go beyond the PG rating in theme, violence, nudity, sensuality, language, adult activities or other elements, but does not reach the restricted R category. The theme of the motion picture by itself will not result in a rating greater than PG-13, although depictions of activities related to a mature theme may result in a restricted rating for the motion picture. Any drug use will initially require at least a PG-13 rating. More than brief nudity will require at least a PG-13 rating, but such nudity in a PG-13 rated motion picture generally will not be sexually oriented. There may be depictions of violence in a PG-13 movie, but generally not both realistic and extreme or persistent violence. A motion picture's single use of one of the harsher sexually-derived words, though only as an expletive, initially requires at least a PG-13 rating. More than one such expletive requires an R rating, as must even one of those words used in a sexual context. The Rating Board nevertheless may rate such a motion picture PG-13 if, based on a special vote by a two-thirds majority, the Raters feel that most American parents would believe that a PG-13 rating is appropriate because of the context or manner in which the words are used or because the use of those words in the motion picture is inconspicuous.
